precepts.text: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as ye see the day approaching.
precepts.point: Separating yourself after receiving the knowledge of the truth is willful sin, and there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, but a fearful looking for of judgment; that is doing despite unto the spirit of grace that woke us up in these last days.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

precepts.why:
Israel is referred to as a camp all through these chapters: the leper, the one with an issue and the one defiled by the dead were put out “without the camp”, “that they defile not their camps, in the midst whereof I dwell.” The Lord is gathering his camp back together again to come and deliver us; if you are not in a camp, get in a camp.

“And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.”

Inside the camp we consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works; the stronger in faith exhort the weaker to keep striving and endure to the end. If you are not gathered you cannot do that, and you do a disservice to the Lord and to your people, and so much the more as we see the day approaching.

precepts.text: Sinning willfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth leaves no more sacrifice for sins, only judgment; the despiser of the covenant is counted worthy of sorer punishment.
precepts.point: Separating yourself after receiving the knowledge of the truth is willful sin, and there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, but a fearful looking for of judgment; that is doing despite unto the spirit of grace that woke us up in these last days.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

precepts.why:
Separating yourself after receiving the knowledge of the truth is willful sin. “For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.”

“He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?”

The despiser of the covenant is counted worthy of sorer punishment than the one who died under Moses’ law. Forsaking the camp after the truth is doing despite unto the spirit of grace that woke us up in these last days; there is no more sacrifice for it, only a fearful looking for of judgment.

precepts.text: Gather yourselves together, O nation not desired; there is nowhere to obey that except gathered in a camp.
precepts.point: Separating yourself after receiving the knowledge of the truth is willful sin, and there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, but a fearful looking for of judgment; that is doing despite unto the spirit of grace that woke us up in these last days.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

precepts.why:
“Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired.” Israel is the nation not desired, and the commandment is to gather. There is nowhere to obey that except gathered in a camp.

The Lord dwelt in the midst of the camp in the wilderness, and he is gathering his camp back together again to come and deliver us. If you are not in a camp, get in a camp.

precepts.text: If any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous, the propitiation for our sins and for the sins of the whole world.
precepts.point: Christ is the advocate and the propitiation, the mercy, for our sins; there is no more Levite priest sacrifice, for he is the mediator between us and the Most High now. The whole world in that verse is the whole world of the nation of Israel.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

precepts.why:
When a man or woman trespassed against the Lord, they confessed their sin and recompensed it with the principal and the fifth part; and if there was no kinsman, the trespass was recompensed “unto the Lord, even to the priest; beside the ram of the atonement.” The atonement now is Christ. We no longer take a ram to a priest, because Christ became the atonement and we ask forgiveness through him.

“My little children, these things write I unto you, that ye sin not. And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous: And he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.”

Christ is the advocate and the propitiation, the mercy, for our sins. There is no more Levite priest sacrifice, for he is the mediator between us and the Most High now. The whole world in that verse is the whole world of the nation of Israel.

precepts.text: Israel shall be saved in the LORD with an everlasting salvation, world without end; that is the whole world the propitiation covers.
precepts.point: Christ is the advocate and the propitiation, the mercy, for our sins; there is no more Levite priest sacrifice, for he is the mediator between us and the Most High now. The whole world in that verse is the whole world of the nation of Israel.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

precepts.why:
Christ is the propitiation for the sins of the whole world, and Isaiah shows which world that is: “But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.”

Israel is saved in the Lord, world without end. That is the whole world the propitiation covers: the whole world of the nation of Israel, whose trespass against the Lord is now atoned for through Christ rather than the ram at the priest’s hand.

precepts.text: Be sure your sin will find you out; nothing done in the dark stays hid before the Most High.
precepts.point: The woman had to answer Amen, amen. If you would not agree to drink the water, you showed yourself guilty already, and the guilty were stoned. Surely your sin shall find you out; there is nothing you can hide.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

precepts.why:
The priest charged the woman by an oath: if no man had lain with her, “be thou free from this bitter water that causeth the curse”; but if she had gone aside to another instead of her husband, “The Lord make thee a curse and an oath among thy people, when the Lord doth make thy thigh to rot, and thy belly to swell.” The Most High is hard on his daughters for a reason, and he was not playing with that judgment.

The woman had to answer “Amen, amen.” If she would not agree to drink the water, she showed herself guilty already, and the guilty were stoned. “But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out.”

There is nothing you can hide. Nothing done in the dark stays hid before the Most High; the bitter water would find out what no man saw.

precepts.text: Put out of the camp every leper, every one that hath an issue, and whosoever is defiled by the dead; that is why those men could not come in.
precepts.point: They asked, wherefore are we kept back, that we may not offer an offering of the Lord in his appointed season? And Moses said, stand still, and I will hear what the Lord will command concerning you.

note.label: Numbers 9: The Second Passover and the Cloud over the Tabernacle

precepts.why:
Certain men “were defiled by the dead body of a man, that they could not keep the passover on that day.” The law had already ruled on them: “And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying, Command the children of Israel, that they put out of the camp every leper, and every one that hath an issue, and whosoever is defiled by the dead.”

Whosoever was defiled by the dead was put out of the camp, so those men could not come in with the congregation to make their offering in his appointed season. That is why they asked, “wherefore are we kept back”, and Moses said, “Stand still, and I will hear what the Lord will command concerning you.”

precepts.text: Put out of the camp every one defiled by the dead; the seven days without the camp keep that law.
precepts.point: Eleazar the priest gave the ordinance: gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead, everything that may abide the fire, goes through the fire and is purified with the water of separation; whatever abides not the fire goes through the water; and on the seventh day they wash their clothes, are clean, and come into the camp.

note.label: Numbers 31: Vengeance on the Midianites

precepts.why:
Those “whosoever hath killed any person, and whosoever hath touched any slain” had to abide without the camp seven days. That is the law going back to the start of the wilderness: “Command the children of Israel, that they put out of the camp every leper, and every one that hath an issue, and whosoever is defiled by the dead.”

The men of war had touched the slain, so they were defiled by the dead and stayed outside the camp until they were purified. The seven days without the camp keep the law of Numbers 5.

points: Every leper, every one that hath an issue, and whosoever is defiled by the dead, male and female, was put out without the camp, that they defile not their camps in the midst whereof the Most High dwelt. And the children of Israel did so.

Inside the camp we consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works; the stronger in faith exhort the weaker to keep striving and endure to the end. If you are not gathered you cannot do that, and you do a disservice to the Lord and to your people.

points: Israel is referred to as a camp all through these chapters. The Lord is gathering his camp back together again to come and deliver us; if you are not in a camp, get in a camp.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

points: When a man or woman commits a trespass against the Lord, they shall confess their sin and recompense the trespass with the principal thereof plus the fifth part, given unto him against whom the trespass was done. Exodus 22 is the chapter of those civil matters and repayments; the Lord laid the payment on you so you would learn not to do it again.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

points: If the man have no kinsman, the trespass was recompensed unto the Lord, even to the priest, beside the ram of the atonement. The atonement now is Christ; we no longer take a ram to a priest, because Christ became the atonement and we ask forgiveness through him.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

points: Every offering of the holy things brought unto the priest was his, because the Levites had no inheritance of land as the other tribes did. Levi was scattered in every land, in Ephraim, in Dan, in Zebulun, in Judah, in Benjamin, so the people could bring the sacrifice to them; Levi had no plot to cultivate crops on, and was fed by the people of the Lord.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

points: If a man's wife go aside and lie with another carnally, hid from the eyes of her husband with no witness, and the spirit of jealousy come upon him, there is a law for it. The spirit of jealousy is the Lord putting it on the husband that something is not right: the routine changes, and he begins questioning and seeing things differently, whether she be defiled or not defiled.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

points: The man brought his wife unto the priest with the tenth part of an ephah of barley meal, no oil and no frankincense upon it, for it is an offering of jealousy, an offering of memorial, bringing iniquity to remembrance; the Lord said do not make this offering sweet.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

points: The priest set the woman before the Lord, took holy water in an earthen vessel with the dust of the floor of the tabernacle, and uncovered the woman's head.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

points: The priest charged her by an oath: if no man have lain with thee, be thou free from this bitter water that causeth the curse; but if thou hast gone aside to another instead of thy husband, the Lord make thy thigh to rot and thy belly to swell. The Most High is hard on his daughters for a reason, and he was not playing with that judgment.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

points: The woman had to answer Amen, amen. If you would not agree to drink the water, you showed yourself guilty already, and the guilty were stoned. Surely your sin shall find you out; there is nothing you can hide.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

points: The priest wrote the curses in a book and blotted them out with the bitter water, waved the jealousy offering before the Lord, burnt the memorial upon the altar, and caused the woman to drink.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

points: If she was defiled, the water became bitter, her belly swelled and her thigh rotted, and the woman became a curse among her people, a plague she could not get rid of. If she was not defiled, she was free and shall conceive seed; the husband was simply tripping, and she was clear.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

points: This is the law of jealousies, when a wife goeth aside or when the spirit of jealousy cometh upon a husband: the priest executed upon her all this law, the man was guiltless from iniquity, and the woman, if guilty, bore her iniquity.
